## 24.1 Memory Layout and Cache Performance

For spatial analysis at national scale — the 73,000+ U.S. census tracts — performance engineering is not optional. The difference between a naive O(n²) algorithm and a properly structured sparse implementation can be the difference between a 10-minute computation and one that never completes. This chapter covers the key Julia performance patterns for large-scale spatial analysis.

```julia
# === Performance profiling workflow ===
# 1. Profile with @profile (flame graph) + ProfileView.jl
using Profile, ProfileView
# Warm up the function first (JIT compilation)
moran(rand(100), test_weights)
# Clear profile data and record
```

### 24.1.1 Threading Spatial Analysis with Threads.@threads

```julia
# 2. Memory allocation profiling
@time moran(rand(3000), us_county_weights)  # Shows time + allocations
@allocated moran(rand(3000), us_county_weights)  # Bytes allocated
# 3. Find the worst offenders
# In flame graph: look for wide bars = CPU time
# @allocated > 0 in hot loops = heap allocation = slow
# ── Key optimization: in-place operations avoid heap allocation ──
# ❌ SLOW: Creates new array on every call (heap allocation)
function moran_slow(x, W)
z   = x .- mean(x)          # Allocates new array
lag = W * z                  # Allocates new array
return dot(z, lag) / dot(z, z) * length(x) / sum(W)
end
# ✅ FAST: Pre-allocated workspace, zero heap allocation in hot path
function moran_fast!(workspace::Vector{Float64}, lag::Vector{Float64},
x::Vector{Float64}, W::SparseMatrixCSC{Float64})
n  = length(x)
x̄  = mean(x)
# In-place: workspace .= x .- x̄  (no allocation)
workspace .= x .- x̄
# In-place sparse matrix-vector product: lag = W*z
mul!(lag, W, workspace)      # SparseArrays mul! is zero-allocation
numerator   = dot(workspace, lag)
denominator = dot(workspace, workspace)
(n / sum(W)) * (numerator / denominator)
end
# Pre-allocate workspace once, reuse for all permutations
workspace = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
lag_buf   = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
# Called 999 times without a single heap allocation:
for _ in 1:999
copyto!(workspace, x)
shuffle!(workspace)
moran_fast!(workspace, lag_buf, workspace, W)
end
# === Multi-threaded LISA computation ===
# LISA is embarrassingly parallel: each location is independent
# Run Julia with: julia -t auto (uses all CPU cores)
function lisa_threaded(
x::Vector{Float64},
w::SpatialWeights;
permutations::Int = 999,
alpha::Float64 = 0.05
)
n  = nobs(w)
x̄  = mean(x)
z  = x .- x̄
m2 = dot(z, z) / n
m2 ≈ 0 && return _constant_lisa(n, alpha)
lag_z   = w.W * z
```

I_local = (z ./ m2) .* lag_z

p_values = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)

```julia
# Each thread gets its own RNG to avoid race conditions
rngs = [MersenneTwister(i) for i in 1:Threads.nthreads()]
# Parallel LISA: each location permuted independently
```
